title: Pentagon says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed
summary: The Pentagon says the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed after War Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be "public."

image.caption: People kneel at the front gate to Fort Hood following a shooting rampage on the grounds Nov. 7, 2009 in Killeen, Texas. The execution by firing squad of the man convicted in the shooting will be livestreamed, the Pentagon said Thursday. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

blocks.text: The Pentagon says the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed after War Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be "public."
Nidal Malik Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people at the military base in 2009
Hegseth, speaking to the conservative TV outlet Real America's Voice News on Wednesday, said the execution of Hasan will take place at Fort Hood on Dec. 3.
Hasan, a former U.S. army officer, was convicted of killing 13 people and injuring 32 others in a shooting at the military base in 2009.
"We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public," Hegseth said.
Hegseth spoke to the outlet aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier while visiting the long-deployed crew, who supported the Iran war, before their arrival at their home port in San Diego.
When asked if Hasan had made any final requests or reached out to the Trump administration, Hegseth simply replied: "Don't care. We'll see him on December 3rd."
Former U.S. major Nidal Hasan, the army psychiatrist convicted in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be executed Dec. 3. (Bell County Sheriff's Office/Getty Images)

Hasan, an army psychiatrist who held the rank of major, walked into a medical building where soldiers were getting checkups, shouted Allahu akbar — Arabic for "God is greater" — and opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun.

During the trial it was revealed that Hasan spent weeks planning the deadly attack, and his preparation included videotaping a sales clerk showing him how to change the magazine on the pistol that he purchased. He would later go to a gun range outside Austin and ask for advice on how to reload with speed and precision from an instructor.
Soldiers later testified that Hasan's rapid reloading made it all but impossible to stop the shooting.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell had said Monday that U.S. President Donald Trump had approved the execution of Hasan.
The White House on Thursday immediately referred questions about the plans for the livestreamed execution to the Pentagon.

items: U.S. army moves to execute man convicted in 2009 deadly Fort Hood rampage by firing squad
Fort Hood massacre trial a rare U.S. military execution case

blocks.text: Officials in the Pentagon clarified Thursday that the execution will be livestreamed and that more details would follow.

The military hasn't executed a servicemember by firing squad since the Second World War. The last military execution took place on April 13, 1961, when Army Private John Bennett was executed by hanging.
